annotations.title: Map what an AI agent may do on its own

description: Use this when someone asks which actions their AI agent or its connected tools may take on their own, which need a person's approval, and which a person must do; or how to set up human oversight, permissions or AI governance for an agent (for example under the EU AI Act). Give either the address of a public MCP server, or the list of tools the agent has (name, description and annotations). Sorts every tool into green (runs alone: reads and prepares), yellow (a person approves: sending, updating, scheduling) or red (a person does it: money, permissions, deletion, code execution, commitments), flags tools with no risk annotations, and returns a ready policy, Claude Code permission rules (allow, ask, deny) and an oversight checklist. Reads tool lists only and never calls a tool. A working checklist, not legal advice.

server_name.description: The name this server has in the agent setup, used in the Claude Code permission rules

tools.description: Instead of an address: the tools the agent has, with their description and annotations

url.description: The MCP server address, for example https://mcp.example.com/mcp

name: map_agent_oversight
